metadata.case_name: SINGH SATNAM v. WONG CHUN FUNG

plaintiff.occupation_before: first owner, then partner in a general store, Dastgeer General Store (specialising in Indian foods and spices)
plaintiff.occupation_after: Unemployed (was employed by his father-in-law at a salary of $5,000.00 per month after return from sick leave)

injuries.description: treated and discharged with a diagnosis of back contusion.
source: treated and discharged with a diagnosis of back contusion.
injuries.icd_description: Contusion of lower back or pelvis
Abrasion of other or unspecified parts of forearm

manifestations.description: continuing and constant low back pain requiring analgesics for pain relief
pain when putting weight on the right foot allowing him to walk no more than 15 minutes before having to rest
difficulty carrying and lifting heavy objects
limited tolerance of sitting and walking and painful trunk movements
some tenderness over his lower back and some reduction in lumbar spine movement with complaint of pain
no significant lower limbs neurological deficit

treatments_received: attended one session of physiotherapy at Queen Elizabeth Hospital
outpatient physiotherapy at Kowloon Hospital (treated on 14 occasions in 2007; in 2008 up to 7 May had attended 23 times)
treatments_future: no further treatment called for apart from use of analgesics when necessary

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: played hockey, which he claims he can no longer do.

losses.category: Loss of sexual function and sexual life
losses.description: can still have sexual activity "but with less power".
enjoyment of life and ability to cope socially will only be mildly affected by his back injury.
limited tolerance of sitting and walking; can walk no more than 15 minutes before having to rest.

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: difficulty carrying and lifting heavy objects affecting his delivery work for the store.

comparable_cases.injury_description: the injuries were more severe, with "moderate" residual pain
